summary: Revenue management, service automation, and demand forecasting lead adoption - and AI assistants are becoming a discovery channel hotels now compete inside of. Who tracks it: the sector's research firms, its standards and trade bodies, and the platforms actually running pricing and guest operations.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Outlook Survey, 8.5% of firms in accommodation and food services, NAICS 72, answered yes to using AI in the last two weeks in the latest period, essentially unchanged from 8.6% in the prior period. The question was first asked in September 2023. That is the sector's measured adoption baseline, and it has not moved much.

What AI is deployed for spans the guest journey and the back office. Per Canary, hospitality software now handles guest messaging, check-in, and operations, with the vendor claiming it improves guest experience, streamlines operations, and boosts revenue across 20,000+ hotels worldwide. The sourced vendor record also places Duetto in revenue management and SevenRooms in guest-experience prediction. On the food-service side, per the National Restaurant Association's tracked automation, Yum Brands deploys voice ordering and kitchen computer vision across its chains, with SoundHound and ConverseNow as the conversational-AI pure-plays taking drive-thru orders. Per Amadeus and Sabre, the global distribution systems apply AI to real-time offer personalization, and per Expedia Group, the OTAs build generative travel planning and price forecasting.

The most consequential shift the sources describe is in discovery. Per HotelWorld AI, its Q1 2026 World's Best at AI Index tracks 2,105+ hotel brands and 131,000 properties globally, measuring who AI engines surface across ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity, and Claude. The report's finding, as carried in the sourced points, is that only a small minority of hotels appear in AI-generated shortlists at all, making answer-engine visibility a tracked competitive metric. Per Skift Research, hotel companies spent the last decade building brand portfolios for coverage and scale, and the next phase of competition will reward sharper brands that drive pricing power, loyalty relevance, and visibility in AI-compressed discovery funnels.

On ROI, the evidence is mostly directional rather than quantified. Canary states its software increases revenue and reduces costs, a vendor claim. Skift Research frames AI as having turned hotel loyalty into a contest on personalization, with no one-size-fits-all strategy, and warns that agentic AI could upend the travel industry. HotelWorld AI describes AI visibility as the industry's next competitive battleground, with travelers asking AI and receiving a shortlist rather than scrolling ten blue links.

The sources are largely silent on AI-specific regulation. AHLA's excerpt centers on advocacy, workforce development, sustainability, and human trafficking prevention, and the National Restaurant Association's excerpt focuses on food safety, utility disruptions, and government relations at every level, with no AI-specific regulatory posture stated. The risk the sources do name is competitive: invisibility in AI-generated recommendations, and the strategic cost of choosing the wrong personalization path.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material suggests a sector where measured adoption is low and flat, but where the distribution and discovery layer is already being reshaped by AI assistants. The practical stakes are visibility in AI shortlists, personalization as a loyalty lever, and agentic AI on the horizon, while the vendor layer, from Canary to the GDS and OTA platforms, is already shipping. The gap between 8.5% measured use and the breadth of deployed vendor capability is the opening.

https://www.ahla.com/.brief: AHLA supports the hotel industry through advocacy, resources, and initiatives that strengthen businesses and the workforce. It runs a voluntary, bipartisan Political Action Committee that helps elect federal candidates who back lodging. The association offers industry-wide connections, events, discounts, updates, and a state-by-state economic impact dashboard, as well as an Allied Attorney Directory. AHLA also pushes legislation on sustainability, workforce development, and human trafficking prevention, and provides policy talking points and best-practice guides. Its membership includes brand companies, owners, management firms, independents, suppliers, and state lodging associations, giving unified advocacy on Capitol Hill and local levels.

https://www.hftp.org/.brief: HFTP, which hosts HITEC, is an international nonprofit association that has been empowering hospitality professionals for “70+ year history” through education, events, networking, research, and skill-building programs. It operates 83 chapters worldwide, including in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Caribbean, UAE, and India. The organization holds a one-day club-professional event each year and a three-day Annual Convention that gathers hundreds of finance and technology professionals for learning, vendor showcases, and networking. HFTP also publishes newsletters such as Hotel Online and Clubs Online, and offers a Corporate Allied Sponsors program to promote companies to its global membership. President James Bina recently shared a letter announcing new resources for members.

https://restaurant.org/.brief: The National Restaurant Association says it helps members build customer loyalty, achieve financial success, and create rewarding careers in foodservice. It offers resources such as a free guide to reduce risk and prepare for public-safety incidents, and a program called “Kids LiveWell” that lets restaurants offer better-for-you meal options to families. The association also publishes a guide titled *Always Ready: Utility Disruptions* to help operators plan for and recover from power, gas, or water outages. It hosts webinars, podcasts, and conferences, including a food-safety webinar with Ecolab experts and a discussion of high-performing beverage categories, and sponsors the Richard E. Marriott Golf Invitational for its Restaurant Advocacy Fund. The site provides the latest news and information aimed at supporting restaurant operations.

https://research.skift.com/.brief: Skift Research's page argues that artificial intelligence has turned hotel loyalty into a contest over personalization, and that no single approach fits every company ,  each hotel group has to work out which path suits it. It also warns that agentic AI could disrupt the travel industry, and points readers to a report titled "Remapping Travel With Agentic AI" for its implications and potential. On branding, the page says hotel companies spent the past decade assembling brand portfolios for coverage and scale, and that the next round of competition will favour sharper brands that generate pricing power, loyalty relevance and visibility as AI compresses how travellers discover options.

https://www.expediagroup.com/.brief: The Expedia Group homepage presents the company as a travel marketplace that connects travelers, partners, and experiences through trusted brands and technology. It says the marketplace offers hotels, vacation rentals, packages, flights, and more, giving travelers many ways to plan and book. The page says, “Expedia Group isn’t just a travel marketplace ,  we’re a catalyst for positive change,” and claims the company aims to create a smarter, more sustainable travel future. It also notes that partners use its B2B technology and advertising solutions to deliver exceptional experiences, and that the company is recognized as a top workplace.
